assumptions: E is a real inner-product space.

steps.title: Rotate in the span of w and z
steps.text: Cosine weights the base direction and sine-over-radius weights the increment.

units.title: A signed great-circle parameterization

assumptions: E is a real inner-product space.

steps.text: Zero velocity gives the constant curve; nonzero velocity gives the signed trigonometric formula.

units.title: Signed sphere geodesics are smooth
units.statement: For fixed base point and velocity, the signed great-circle curve is continuously differentiable to every requested finite order.
assumptions: E is a real inner-product space.

units.title: Forward exponential steps equal the signed geodesic

assumptions: t is nonnegative.
Zero time and zero velocity are allowed.

units.title: Tangent exponential steps remain on the unit sphere
units.statement: A unit base point and an orthogonal increment produce an exponential-map value with exactly unit norm.
assumptions: E is a real inner-product space.
z=0 is allowed.

units.title: Second derivative at a local minimum
units.statement: For a real function continuous at a local minimum, the second derivative represented by deriv (deriv f) is nonnegative.
units.formula: x\text{ local min of }f,\ f\text{ continuous at }x\Longrightarrow (\operatorname{deriv}\operatorname{deriv}f)(x)\ge0
assumptions: f is a real-valued function on the real line.
x is a local minimum of f.
f is continuous at x; Mathlib deriv is total and equals zero at nondifferentiable points.

steps.title: Rule out a negative second derivative
steps.text: If the second derivative were negative, Mathlib’s strict second-derivative test would also make x a local maximum.
steps.formula: f^{\prime\prime}(x)<0\Longrightarrow x\text{ is a local maximum}
steps.lean: Use isLocalMax_of_deriv_deriv_neg, with Fermat’s identity at the local minimum.

steps.title: Combine the two local inequalities
steps.text: A point that is both a local minimum and a local maximum has a neighborhood on which f is constant.
steps.lean: Intersect the two neighborhood filters and apply antisymmetry.

steps.title: Differentiate the local equality twice
steps.text: The derivative is locally zero, hence its derivative at x is zero, contradicting strict negativity.
steps.formula: f\equiv f(x)\text{ locally}\Longrightarrow f^\prime\equiv0\text{ locally}\Longrightarrow f^{\prime\prime}(x)=0
steps.lean: Filter.EventuallyEq.deriv and deriv_eq transport the local equality.

units.title: Second derivative at a local maximum
units.statement: For a real function continuous at a local maximum, the second derivative represented by deriv (deriv f) is nonpositive.
units.formula: x\text{ local max of }f,\ f\text{ continuous at }x\Longrightarrow (\operatorname{deriv}\operatorname{deriv}f)(x)\le0
assumptions: f is a real-valued function on the real line.
x is a local maximum of f.
f is continuous at x; Mathlib deriv is total and equals zero at nondifferentiable points.

steps.title: Rule out a positive second derivative
steps.text: A positive second derivative and Fermat’s identity would make x a local minimum.
steps.formula: f^{\prime\prime}(x)>0\Longrightarrow x\text{ is a local minimum}
steps.lean: Use isLocalMin_of_deriv_deriv_pos.

steps.title: Force local constancy
steps.text: The local minimum and maximum inequalities agree, so f equals f(x) near x.
steps.lean: Intersect the two filters and apply order antisymmetry.

steps.title: Contradict strict positivity
steps.text: Differentiating the local constant germ twice gives second derivative zero.
steps.lean: Use the congruence theorem for deriv twice.
